body: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

summaryZh: 理解大模型（LLM）的社会智能对于人机交互和多智能体环境中的应用日益重要。社会智能包含两个方面：认知智能，即推断他人心理状态的能力；行为智能，即根据这些推理选择适当社会行动以实现社会目标的能力。说服过程提供了一个天然的测试平台，但先前的基准通常使用合成场景孤立地评估它们。为此，本文推出了PerSo基准，利用Reddit的ChangeMyView社区中真实的说服对话，并通过LLM闭环流程构建、经人工注释验证的方案来评估这两方面。对多样化LLM的评估表明，模型性能通常随模型规模扩展，但在各个维度上存在差异。最强模型在行为任务上略微超过了最佳人类表现，而最佳人类参与者在认知任务上仍保持领先。
